binders: A set V of n vertices.
conclusions: The Erdos-Renyi model G(n,p) is the random graph on V obtained by deciding independently for every pair of distinct vertices whether that pair is an edge, with edge probability p for each pair.
Equivalently, the edge indicators indexed by distinct vertex pairs are jointly independent Bernoulli(p) random variables.
definitions_and_conventions: G(n,p) names the random-graph model/distribution, while notation of the form G distributed as G(n,p) denotes a random graph sampled from it.
Candidate edges correspond to pairs of distinct vertices, so self-loops are excluded.
The nearby degree calculation treats each incident-edge indicator as Ber(p) and counts n-1 such indicators for a fixed vertex.
implicit_context: The word probability implicitly places p in the probability interval, though the source does not display a separate range assumption here.
The ordinary graph language and use of vertex pairs indicate the standard simple undirected graph model.
The source does not require a particular labeling of the n-element vertex set.

details: Every candidate edge has the same inclusion probability p.
No distinct vertex pair is omitted from the random construction.
Edge choices for the distinct vertex pairs are mutually independent, not merely pairwise specified by their marginal probabilities.
The vertex set has exactly n elements.
Edges join distinct vertices; self-loops are not candidate edges.
G(n,p) is a random-graph law or model from which a graph G may be sampled.

undebatable_constraints: The model must be defined on a vertex set of cardinality n.
Every pair of distinct vertices must be a candidate edge.
Each candidate edge must be present with probability p.
The candidate-edge choices must be independent across vertex pairs.
The construction must exclude self-loops by restricting to distinct vertices.

contract_plain_english: The Erdos-Renyi model G(n,p) is a random graph on a set of n vertices. For each pair of distinct vertices, include the edge with probability p, independently of all the other vertex pairs. Thus its edge indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) variables, with no self-loops.
